## TOYO Co., Ltd Announces Unaudited Third Quarter and First Nine Months 2026 Financial Results


November 16, 2026


TOKYO


, Nov. 16, 2026


/PRNewswire/ -- TOYO Co., Ltd (Nasdaq: TOYO) (OTC: TOYWF) ("TOYO," "we" or the "Company"), a solar manufacturing company, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter of 2026 and the nine months ended September 30, 2026.


**Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights**


- 634.7 MW of solar cells and 277.4 MW of solar modules delivered
- Revenues of $129.0 million, compared to $135.6 million in the third quarter of 2025, a decrease of 4.8%, and an increase of 9.2% from $118.2 million in the second quarter of 2026
- Revenues from third parties of $112.1 million, an increase of 57.3% year-over-year
- Gross margin of 16.6%, compared to 25.7% in the third quarter of 2025 and 31.3% in the second quarter of 2026
- Net income of $4.3 million, compared to $22.6 million in the third quarter of 2025


- Adjusted EBITDA (Non-GAAP) of $19.5 million
- Adjusted Net Income (Non-GAAP) of $4.5 million
- Earnings per share, basic and diluted, of $0.10, compared to $0.66 in the third quarter of 2025


**First Nine Months 2026 Financial Highlights**


- 3.25 GW of solar cells and 469.0 MW of solar modules delivered
- Revenues of $390.0 million, an increase of 42.0% year-over-year
- Gross margin of 27.2%, compared to 21.1% in the first nine months of 2025
- Net income of $50.1 million, compared to $25.1 million in the first nine months of 2025, an increase of 99.5% year-over-year
- Adjusted EBITDA (Non-GAAP) of $102.1 million
- Adjusted Net Income (Non-GAAP) of $50.7 million
- Earnings per share of $1.27 basic and $1.26 diluted, compared to $0.66 in the first nine months of 2025


"We continued to expand our U.S. manufacturing platform and remained profitable through a quarter shaped by an evolving and challenging trade environment," said Takahiko Onozuka, Chairman and CEO of TOYO. "With our second solar module line in the Houston area now operational, third-party revenue up 57.3% and nine-month total revenue up 42.0% year-over-year, we are strengthening our domestic production base to meet the growing demand from U.S. customers. We are also actively exploring opportunities to manufacture wafers in the United States, as part of building a more integrated domestic supply chain."


"Demand for U.S.-made solar modules from a transparent, non-FEOC (Foreign Entity of Concern) supply chain remains strong. Our Houston solar module capacity now stands at approximately 2 GW with our second line completed, is substantially committed for 2027," said Rhone Resch, Chief Strategy Officer of TOYO. "We welcome the Trump Administration's Section 232 action and will continue our negotiations with the U.S. Department of Commerce to strengthen solar manufacturing in the United States through our planned heterojunction (HJT) solar cell line and potential expansion into upstream solar products."


**Cash Flow and Liquidity**


Cash from operations was $35.2 million, and capital expenditures were $44.1 million for the first nine months of 2026. As of September 30, 2026, the Company had $74.0 million of cash and restricted cash, compared to $58.9 million as of December 31, 2025. Working capital, defined as current assets less current liabilities, was approximately $46.3 million as of September 30, 2026.


**Business Update**


- **Approximately $240 million in U.S. solar module supply agreements.** Since mid-June 2026, TOYO has entered into multiple binding solar module supply agreements with U.S. customers, with an aggregate contract value of approximately $240 million. Deliveries under these agreements began in the third quarter of 2026 and are scheduled to continue through the first half of 2027.
- **2 GW Houston-area, Texas solar module facility inaugurated.** On October 6, 2026, TOYO held a ribbon-cutting ceremony at its Houston-area facility, Texas, marking the completion of its expansion of solar module nameplate capacity to 2 GW. The ceremony was attended by government, community, and industry leaders, including Jeffrey I. Kessler, Under Secretary of Commerce for Industry and Security, Takeshi Koyama, Consul General of Japan in Houston, Congressman Christian D. Menefee, and Paul Wormser, Senior Vice President of CEA Intertek, along with customers, partners, analysts, and investors.
- **1.5 GW HJT solar cell line.** TOYO continues to develop its 1.5 GW HJT solar cell line at its Houston-area site in Humble, Texas, representing a $357 million investment, with pilot production expected no later than the first quarter of 2028.
- **Ethiopia operations and trade proceedings.** Third-quarter shipments of solar cells from TOYO's Ethiopia facility were affected by a U.S. Customs and Border Protection ("CBP") examination. All shipments affected by that examination have subsequently been released. TOYO is also pursuing certification under CBP's Customs Trade Partnership Against Terrorism ("CTPAT") program to further strengthen the security and transparency of its supply chain .


The release of those shipments does not resolve the separate U.S. Department of Commerce ("Commerce") circumvention inquiry concerning solar cells completed in Ethiopia, which was initiated on July 17, 2026 and remains ongoing. TOYO is cooperating fully with the inquiry and providing complete documentation relating to its supply chain.
- **Section 232 proclamation on polysilicon and solar products.** On August 6, 2026, the Trump Administration issued a proclamation under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 on imports of polysilicon and downstream solar products (the "Section 232 program"). TOYO welcomed the action and has submitted a proposal to the Department of Commerce for an offset agreement that would support Commerce's multi-year integrated U.S. investment plan in advanced manufacturing to support onshoring of the U.S. solar and semiconductor supply chain. TOYO is currently in negotiations with Commerce on the terms of the offset agreement.


**Guidance**


With TOYO's Houston solar module capacity substantially committed for 2027, the Company expects its Texas solar module operations to run at or near full capacity next year. Shipments of solar cells from TOYO's Ethiopia facility continue to be affected by the policy environment. Because this environment remains dynamic, TOYO is taking a cautious approach and is not updating its outlook or providing specific guidance on revenue, net income or other financial metrics at this time.

**About TOYO Co., Ltd.**


TOYO is a solar manufacturing company that is committed to becoming a vertically integrated solar manufacturer in the global market, integrating the upstream production of wafers and silicon, midstream production of solar cells, downstream production of photovoltaic modules, and potentially other stages of the solar power supply chain. TOYO is well-positioned to produce high-quality solar cells and modules at a competitive scale and cost.

TOYO believes these non-GAAP measures of financial results provide useful information to management and investors regarding certain financial and business trends relating to TOYO's financial condition and results of operations. TOYO's management uses these non-GAAP measures for trend analysis and for budgeting and planning purposes. TOYO believes that the use of these non-GAAP measures provides an additional tool for investors to evaluate projected operating results and trends, as well as compare TOYO's financial measures with those of other similar companies, many of which also present similar non-GAAP financial measures to investors.


Management of TOYO does not consider these non-GAAP measures in isolation or as an alternative to financial measures determined in accordance with GAAP. The principal limitation of these non-GAAP financial measures is that they exclude significant expenses such as share-based compensation and changes in fair value of contingent consideration and income that are required by GAAP to be recorded in TOYO's financial statements. In addition, they are subject to inherent limitations as they reflect the exercise of judgments by management about which expenses and income are excluded or included in determining these non-GAAP financial measures. You should review TOYO's audited and unaudited financial statements filed with the SEC and not rely on any single financial measure to evaluate TOYO's business, results of operations and financial condition.
